headline: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals 40% cost-savings gap for enterprise Claude users
summary: Despite Anthropic's reported revenue run-rate soaring to $47B, 40% of enterprise customers using Claude report less than 10% cost savings, signaling potential pricing adjustments.
details: Anthropic has confidentially filed for an IPO, with reports suggesting a post-money valuation of $965B after a $65B Series H raise. The company's revenue run-rate is reportedly $47B, a significant increase from $9B at the end of 2025.

However, a notable challenge emerges: 40% of enterprise customers indicate they achieved under 10% cost savings from their Claude deployments. This stark contrast between rapid revenue growth and perceived value suggests an impending re-pricing event.

The core issue is an 'accounting mismatch' where users pay per invocation but derive value per completed goal. This leads to hidden costs from retries, dead-end agent branches, and unverified completions that consume tokens without delivering results.

These inefficiencies don't appear as obvious line items but contribute to bills that are disproportionately high compared to actual productive work. Public markets prioritize margin, creating an incentive for vendors to adjust pricing on currently subsidized tiers.

The article advises against hastily switching AI vendors, as migrating an agent stack is costly and other providers face similar per-invocation versus per-goal challenges. The focus should instead be on implementing robust cost controls.

Effective strategies include capping spend and verifying goal completion before payment. Tools like AgentGuard, a runtime budget limiter for AI agents, allow users to set budgets per goal and track token usage with an audit trail.

This approach ensures agents operate under a hard ceiling, stopping before quietly burning money on unproductive paths. Per-goal accounting transforms vague cost concerns into measurable data, highlighting exactly where resources are being consumed inefficiently.

headline_marked: [[Intel's 'Raptor Lake Next' reportedly features up to 20 cores]] and retains Core 200 branding
headline: Intel's 'Raptor Lake Next' reportedly features up to 20 cores and retains Core 200 branding
summary: The upcoming CPU lineup, slated for early 2027, is rumored to land on the LGA 1700 socket and include a special 10-core SKU with 24MB of L3 cache.
details: Intel's third Raptor Lake refresh, codenamed "Raptor Lake Next," is reportedly in the works for an early 2027 release. Leaks from tipster Jaykihn suggest it will retain the LGA 1700 socket and existing Core 200 branding.

This new lineup is expected to utilize Raptor Lake silicon, not Bartlett Lake, confirming a hybrid P-core and E-core configuration. It will scale across desktop and mobile platforms with up to 125W HX models, but without introducing any new features.

Essentially, these CPUs appear to be rebranded 14th Gen processors, likely re-released to maximize returns on high-yield silicon. Intel invested significant effort in stabilizing the 13th and 14th Gen families, making this a strategic move.

The rumored lineup will reportedly span Core 3, Core 5, and Core 7 SKUs, with no Core 9 parts initially. The top Core 7 variant is said to feature 8 P-cores and 12 E-cores, totaling 20 cores at 65W, similar to the Core i7-14700.

A Core 5 part is listed with 16 cores (8 P-cores + 8 E-cores) at 125W, resembling the Core i7-13700K. Additionally, a unique 10-core 65W SKU with an increased 24MB of L3 cache is expected, alongside a Core 3 CPU with 4 P-cores and no E-cores, also at 65W.

All Raptor Lake Next chips will use Raptor Cove P-cores and Gracemont E-cores. They will retain Intel HD 700 series integrated graphics and support DDR4 memory, leveraging the LGA 1700 platform, which could offer a more budget-friendly PC build option.

Production is anticipated to begin in January 2027, with availability in Q1 2027. This lineup is expected to coexist with Nova Lake, potentially serving as Intel's value-focused offering, making the Core 200 vs. Core 400 distinction important for consumers.
